name: ICD 705 SCIF-Grade Construction
description: Facility construction to ICD 705 / ICS 705-1 standards: complete physical enclosures (walls, floor, ceiling as continuous barrier), RF shielding, acoustic attenuation (Sound Group 3-4), no windows, all utility penetrations maintaining perimeter integrity.

current_state.summary: Standard for government classified facilities for decades. No AI lab has built a SCIF-grade datacenter. Specialized contractors exist but the intersection with AI-scale datacenter requirements (cooling, power density) is novel.

technical_feasibility.notes: Proven technology with decades of government construction experience, but the AI-scale version is not yet demonstrated. The Utah Data Center - the usual parallel - is roughly 65MW at about 1M sq ft, took around 3.5 years and overran its budget, which is the right order of magnitude for the enclave this block prices but well below a full training campus. Passing tens to hundreds of MW of power and liquid cooling through a continuous shielded envelope is the genuinely unproven part.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Site selection, permitting, specialised construction, then accreditation. Cannot be rushed below 18 months for a small facility. Conventional GW-scale AI campuses already take 1-3.6 years to first power; SCIF-grade adds 15-30% schedule drag plus accreditation, which has stretched toward 24-36 months under the updated standards and is a government-controlled dependency that money cannot compress. Retrofitting is much harder than new construction.

cost.notes: Prices the SECURITY PREMIUM for a secure enclave, not a whole datacenter. A lab builds the compute facility regardless, so what this control costs is the delta for classified-grade construction: commercial AI datacenter runs $15-20M/MW and AWS's classified buildout implies roughly $38M/MW, making the attributable premium about $20M/MW. The unit is a 50-100MW enclave holding weights at rest - the same scope NET-02 assumes - not the entire training fleet, which does not need to sit inside a shielded envelope. 50-100MW at a $15-23M/MW premium gives this range. Per square foot SCIF construction ($350-1,200) and AI datacenter construction ($1,100-1,500) are comparable; the premium comes from cleared labour, 15-30% schedule drag and security-driven rework. Ongoing covers accreditation maintenance, a dedicated security force and integrity checks. Building the whole campus to this grade would be several times larger and is not what SL5 requires.

vendor_dependency.notes: Specialized contractors required. Government cooperation may be needed for accreditation.

supply_scarcity.bottleneck: SCIF-certified construction contractors who also understand datacenter-scale cooling and power
supply_scarcity.notes: These two expertise areas rarely overlap. Need to pair SCIF contractors with datacenter engineers.

organizational_readiness.notes: AI labs have zero experience with classified facility construction. This is the most alien block culturally. Requires bringing in entirely new expertise.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without SCIF-grade construction, physical intrusion, eavesdropping through walls, TEMPEST collection from EM emissions, and acoustic surveillance are all viable. Standard datacenter security focuses on preventing theft of hardware, not preventing sophisticated signals intelligence collection.

completed_by.why: ICD 705 pairs the physical shell with detection and a response time for a reason: a continuous barrier nobody is watching just means an intruder who gets in has unlimited time.

open_questions.question: Can AI-scale power and cooling requirements (potentially 5-10 GW per facility by 2029) be met within SCIF construction constraints?
open_questions.impact_if_resolved_negatively: May need novel SCIF-grade cooling approaches or accept smaller facility scale

open_questions.question: Private self-certification (CSO/Site Security Manager) vs government accreditation: does private accreditation provide meaningful security assurance?
open_questions.impact_if_resolved_negatively: Government accreditation required — adds timeline and access constraints

real_world_parallels.description: NSA's Utah Data Center (2013) is a SCIF-grade facility at datacenter scale — proving the concept is feasible. It houses classified computing at massive scale with full ICD 705 compliance.

name: TEMPEST Countermeasures
description: RF shielding preventing electromagnetic signal egress from computing areas, plus dedicated power conditioning preventing power-line analysis. Per NSTISSAM TEMPEST/1-92. All equipment hardwired — no wireless devices permitted.

current_state.summary: Integral to SCIF construction (PHY-01). Cannot be deployed independently without facility-grade shielding. Individual TEMPEST-rated equipment exists but facility-level protection requires construction.

technical_feasibility.notes: Mature technology. Part of ICD 705 construction. The AI-specific concern is whether models can deliberately modulate emissions — but physical shielding works regardless of intent.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Bundled with PHY-01 SCIF construction. Cannot be deployed faster than the facility itself.

cost.notes: Scales with the shielded floor area of PHY-01 rather than being a fixed line item, so it tracks the enclave rather than the whole campus. Must be engineered into construction: retrofitting is possible but degraded, since existing penetrations and legacy routing make shielding continuity hard to achieve. Estimate is directional - facility-scale TEMPEST pricing is not published.

vendor_dependency.notes: Specialized vendors required but market exists.

supply_scarcity.bottleneck: TEMPEST engineers who understand both RF shielding and AI datacenter EM profiles
supply_scarcity.notes: TEMPEST expertise exists in government space; AI datacenter EM profiles are novel

organizational_readiness.notes: No WiFi, no Bluetooth, no wireless anything in Red Zones. Major operational impact for people accustomed to modern connectivity.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without TEMPEST countermeasures, an adversary outside the facility (or in an adjacent uncontrolled space) can use sensitive equipment to capture electromagnetic emissions and reconstruct data being processed. AI models could potentially encode data into EM patterns deliberately.

completed_by.why: TEMPEST countermeasures assume the emitters are the ones you shielded. A phone or wireless keyboard inside the shielded space, or a shell with uncontrolled penetrations, re-opens the channel the shielding closed.

open_questions.question: TEMPEST zone classification for Red Zones: what zone (1, 2, or 3) is appropriate?
open_questions.impact_if_resolved_negatively: Higher zones = more expensive and restrictive construction requirements

real_world_parallels.description: During the Cold War, the Soviets placed a resonant cavity bugging device ("The Thing") inside a gift to the US ambassador — demonstrating that EM emissions and RF devices can be weaponized for espionage at the highest levels.

name: Access Control Vestibules (Mantraps)
description: Interlocking door systems at all Red Zone entry/exit points. Two sets of doors that cannot be open simultaneously, with multi-factor authentication and anti-tailgating sensors. Prevents unauthorized personnel from following authorized personnel through doors.

current_state.summary: Standard feature in high-security facilities. Some AI labs have basic mantraps at datacenter entrances. Full implementation at all Red Zone boundaries with anti-tailgating requires more pervasive deployment.

technical_feasibility.notes: Completely proven, widely available commercial products. No technical uncertainty.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Installation is straightforward. Longer if retrofitting into existing buildings without space for vestibules.

cost.notes: Per-entry-point cost × number of entry points. Lower cost relative to other physical blocks.

vendor_dependency.notes: Multiple vendors, competitive market, commodity product.

organizational_readiness.notes: Minor convenience impact. Most tech companies already have badge access; mantraps add 15-30 seconds per entry.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without mantraps, an adversary can tailgate an authorized employee through a badge-access door. This is the simplest physical access attack — requires no technology, just social engineering or waiting for someone to hold the door.

real_world_parallels.description: Every SCIF facility worldwide uses mantraps. The 2019 Mar-a-Lago intrusion attempt was stopped by a mantrap-equivalent access control point.

name: Intrusion Detection Systems (5/15-min Response)
description: Intrusion detection to ICD 705 standards with alarm response by an armed reaction force. Response time depends on security-in-depth: open storage requires response within 15 minutes where SID is present, or 5 minutes where it is not; closed storage requires 15 minutes. Continuous monitoring of all Red Zone boundaries.

current_state.summary: Standard datacenter security has cameras and badge systems. ICD 705-grade IDS with guaranteed 5-minute armed response is government-level and not deployed by AI labs. Requires dedicated security force.

technical_feasibility.notes: Proven technology. Sensors, cameras, alarm systems are commodity. The challenge is the response guarantee — 5-minute armed response requires on-site security force 24/7.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Sensor installation is fast. Hiring, training, and retaining 24/7 armed security force takes longer.

cost.notes: Dominated by the guard force rather than the sensors. A facility with strong perimeter security-in-depth (which PHY-01, PHY-03 and PHY-06 provide) qualifies for the 15-minute response standard rather than 5 minutes, which is a materially cheaper staffing model - so the companion controls change this block's ongoing cost, not just its effectiveness.

vendor_dependency.notes: Commodity sensors. Guard force can be contracted or internal.

supply_scarcity.bottleneck: Trained armed security personnel willing to work datacenter sites (often remote)
supply_scarcity.notes: Security guard labor market exists but quality varies. Need higher caliber for SL5.

organizational_readiness.notes: Armed guards at a tech company is culturally jarring. But datacenter physical security is an accepted practice — just needs to be upgraded.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without rapid-response IDS, a physical intruder has unlimited time once past the perimeter. Even a detected intrusion is meaningless if response time is 30-60 minutes — an adversary can install implants, copy data, or cause damage within that window.

real_world_parallels.description: Nuclear facilities maintain armed response forces with 5-minute response requirements under NRC regulations. The same concept applies — high-value assets requiring rapid physical protection.

name: No Wireless Devices in Red Zones
description: Complete prohibition of wireless devices (WiFi, Bluetooth, cellular, NFC) inside Red Zones. All equipment hardwired with wireless capabilities physically removed or disabled. No phones, no wireless keyboards/mice, no wireless headsets.

current_state.summary: Standard SCIF requirement. Enforced in government classified facilities universally. Not enforced in any AI lab — would be highly disruptive to current work culture.

technical_feasibility.notes: Not a technology problem — it's a policy and enforcement problem. Hardwired alternatives exist for everything.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Policy creation and enforcement infrastructure (RF detection, device lockers at entries, hardwired replacements). Fast if org is willing.

cost.notes: Device lockers, RF detection systems, hardwired equipment replacements, enforcement staff. Low relative to other blocks.

organizational_readiness.notes: Extremely culturally disruptive for tech workers accustomed to phones and wireless everything. This is one of the hardest blocks to implement purely due to human resistance.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Wireless devices are covert exfiltration channels. A compromised phone can record audio, photograph screens, or relay data. Wireless implants (keyboard loggers, RF beacons) can be planted and transmit to nearby receivers. RF emissions from wireless devices can interfere with TEMPEST countermeasures.

real_world_parallels.description: Every SCIF worldwide prohibits personal electronic devices. Employees leave phones in lockers outside the secured area. This has been standard practice for the intelligence community since mobile phones became ubiquitous.

name: Zone Architecture (Red Zone / Black Zone)
description: Formal division of facilities into Red Zones (where SL5-protected information may be processed/stored, full security controls) and Black Zones (no network path to SL5 information, standard security). All SL5 Network hardware must be within Red Zones.

current_state.summary: Concept exists in government (classified vs unclassified areas). AI labs have informal segmentation (server rooms vs offices) but not the formal Red/Black zone architecture with enforced separation.

technical_feasibility.notes: Well-understood architecture. Challenge is defining exactly which systems need Red Zone placement and managing the operational boundary.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Requires facility redesign, system relocation, boundary definition, and policy implementation. Easier in new construction than retrofit.

cost.notes: Physical construction of zone boundaries, access control systems, monitoring. Ongoing = maintaining zone integrity and access policies.

vendor_dependency.notes: Standard construction with security requirements. No exotic vendors needed.

supply_scarcity.bottleneck: Security architects experienced in zone design for large-scale computing
supply_scarcity.notes: Government security architects can advise but need datacenter context

organizational_readiness.notes: Researchers accustomed to walking freely to any server must now badge into specific zones. Creates physical friction in daily work.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without formal zone architecture, there's no clear physical boundary between sensitive and non-sensitive systems. An adversary who gains access to any part of the facility may be able to physically reach weight-storing systems without additional barriers.

completed_by.why: A Red/Black split is a line on a floor plan until something enforces the crossing. Vestibules and a real construction boundary are what make the zone a boundary rather than a designation.

real_world_parallels.description: The NSA campus at Fort Meade separates areas by classification level. Personnel badge into each zone, with increasing restrictions at higher zones. The same principle applied to AI datacenters.

name: Multi-Modal Hardware Inspection Pipeline
description: Systematic inspection of all hardware components before installation and periodically thereafter. Multi-modal: X-ray imaging, infrared thermography, computer vision comparison against baseline, random destructive evaluation. Detects implants, counterfeits, and tampering.

current_state.summary: Government uses some inspection techniques for classified hardware. No AI lab performs systematic hardware inspection beyond basic visual checks. The full multi-modal pipeline at datacenter scale is novel.

technical_feasibility.notes: Individual techniques exist (X-ray, IR). Scaling to datacenter volumes (thousands of components) with automated detection is engineering challenge. Ptychographic laminography for highest assurance is cutting-edge.

time_to_deploy_months.notes: Equipment procurement, lab setup, process development, staff training. The random destructive evaluation component requires accepting cost of destroying some hardware.

cost.notes: Inspection equipment + lab + staff + destroyed components. Ongoing cost scales with hardware procurement volume.

vendor_dependency.notes: Equipment available commercially. May outsource to specialized labs initially.

supply_scarcity.bottleneck: Hardware inspection specialists who can interpret X-ray/IR results for modern semiconductors
supply_scarcity.notes: Rare skill set — mostly exists in government counterintelligence and defense contractors

organizational_readiness.notes: Adds time to hardware procurement pipeline. Requires accepting that some % of expensive hardware will be deliberately destroyed for verification.

adversary_exploitation.exploit_narrative: Without hardware inspection, a supply chain compromise (compromised chip with hardware backdoor) goes undetected. The implant arrives through legitimate channels, passes standard acceptance testing, and operates normally until activated by the adversary.

open_questions.question: Can automated inspection scale to datacenter hardware volumes without unacceptable procurement delays?
open_questions.impact_if_resolved_negatively: Must rely on sampling rather than exhaustive inspection — reduces detection probability

real_world_parallels.description: The US DoD's Trusted Foundry program inspects semiconductor components for military systems. The process includes die-level imaging and comparison against golden references.
